_comment: BUILDINGS THE MAP DOES NOT HAVE.
Every footprint in this world comes from OpenStreetMap, and once in a while
OSM simply has no building where a building plainly stands. Not a bad tag, not
a wrong height -- nothing at all. That is not something a height override or a
recipe can fix, because a recipe needs a footprint to be called with.
This file is the exception list, and it is deliberately small and deliberately
noisy about provenance. Every entry must cite the research that measured it.
An entry here is a claim that a real building exists at a real place at a real
size, and if that claim is wrong the world is worse than the hole was.
Shapes are stored as PARAMETERS, not as vertex lists: a centre, radii and arc
spans are readable, auditable and correctable, where 140 projected lat/lon
pairs are none of those things.

buildings.src: research/chinatown-landmarks.md B.3. OSM has NO building footprint here -- way 295892200 is landuse=residential and still carries a wikipedia link to Pearl Bank Apartments, which was demolished Feb-Mar 2020. One Pearl Bank topped out Dec 2024 and is the tallest residential building in Outram-Chinatown, so the model had a hole where it stands. R=46.0m is a least-squares circle fit to the roof's outer edge over a ~145deg arc, rms 2.13m over 142 sample points, taken on the NORTH arc where the satellite lean is tangential. Ring outer diameter ~92m fills the site's 93m N-S dimension, which is an independent confirmation. Tower depth 16m is [EST] range 13-18. Two free-standing crescents that do NOT interlock; they touch only at roof level via sky bridges. One gap is confidently E to SSE where the entry court, porte-cochere and pool are; the opposite gap could not be pinned and is placed symmetrically.
buildings.h_src: 135m above its own platform, [EST] range 128-145. The widely repeated 178m is NOT a height above local ground: 178/39 storeys = 4.56m per floor, which no residential building has. Pearl's Hill stands ~43m, and 178-43 = 135 gives 3.46m per storey, which fits. Putting a 178m box on the terrain would make this building ~40m too tall.

buildings.src: research/authored-footprints.md D.2-D.3. OSM way 47126585 EXISTS but carries construction=yes and NO building tag, so build_district.py's way["building"] query never fetches it -- and it also sits at lon 103.8644-103.8658, outside the bugis east edge of 103.8640. Two independent reasons the most famous building on Beach Road was missing. It is NOT demolished: URA gazetted it for conservation 22 Oct 2021 and that was the condition of the May 2022 en-bloc; it is gutted and hoarded while being restored, with a 45-storey tower going up alongside for late 2029. Confirmed standing in ESRI WorldView-2 imagery captured 2025-05-07. Plan geometry is MEASURED on the OSM way, not on pixels: 9,289 m2 over 40 vertices, long-axis bearing 50.9 deg by PCA, 178.4m along by 68.8m across. The baseline here is the straight NW back face fronting Beach Road (151.8m); the terraces face SE toward Nicoll Highway, which was measured from a perpendicular luminance profile, not assumed.
buildings.h_src: 89m [PUBLISHED] from DP Architects' own project page -- first-party, the architect. FLAGGED, NOT TRUSTED BLIND: the same sources say 16 storeys, and 89/16 = 5.56m per storey, which no residential-over-retail building has. Same shape of error as the 178m repeated for One Pearl Bank. The alternative is 55-62m [UNPUBLISHED/ESTIMATE]. A shadow measurement could not settle it -- the sun azimuth was only 17 deg off the slab's own axis, so it back-solved to 48-70m with an error bar too wide to overturn the architect. Built at 89 on the research's own recommendation, because for a 178 x 64m slab a height error reads far less badly than a wrong position or orientation. If it ends up towering over Golden Mile Tower, drop to 60.
